title: Verbal Fluency and Mental-State Recognition in Ecuadorian Adults: Evidence of a Lexical-Cognitive Association in Social Cognition.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Verbal fluency (VF) is a neuropsychological measure sensitive to lexical-semantic organization and prefrontal circuits. Its link with social cognition-specifically with the recognition of mental states from the eyes-remains scarcely explored in Latin American contexts.
OBJECTIVE: To examine the association between performance on the Verbal Fluency Test (phonological and semantic) and mental-state recognition, as measured by the Reading the Mind in the Eyes Test (RMET) in Ecuadorian adults, controlling for sociodemographic variables.
METHOD: A cross-sectional correlational study with 397 healthy adults (Mage = 36.8 years,= 11.5; range: 18-83; 219 women, 178 men) assessed in Quito, Ecuador, using the multidomain ECUACOG neuropsychological battery. Pearson's correlations with 95% CIs, Spearman's correlations, the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, one-way ANOVA with η, Tukey's HSD post hoc comparisons, and simple linear regressions were computed.
RESULTS: Total VF was significantly associated with RMET score (= 0.227, 95% CI [0.131, 0.319],< 0.001,= 390). Semantic VF showed a higher correlation than phonological VF (= 0.239, 95% CI [0.144, 0.331] vs.= 0.163, 95% CI [0.065, 0.258]; Steiger's= 1.86,= 0.063, non-significant trend). Educational level was associated with both VF (semantic VF: η= 0.093,< 0.001) and RMET (η= 0.045,< 0.001) scores. The semantic VF-RMET association remained significant after statistically controlling for TMT-B and for educational level (partial= 0.202,< 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Lexical-semantic richness is significantly associated with mental-state recognition in Ecuadorian adults. These findings contribute to the generation of neuropsychological normative data in Ecuador.
